questions.stem: India's climate is predominantly classified as:
questions.explanation: India has a tropical monsoon climate, characterised by seasonal reversal of winds and concentration of rainfall in summer (June-September).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The South-West Monsoon typically reaches the Kerala coast by:
questions.explanation: Normal date of South-West Monsoon onset over Kerala: approximately 1 June. It then progresses northwards, covering the entire country by mid-July.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Mawsynram and Cherrapunji (Meghalaya) receive the highest rainfall in India because:

options.option_text: They lie in the windward side of the Khasi Hills and receive orographic rainfall from Bay of Bengal branch of monsoon
They are adjacent to the Arabian Sea
They are in a rain shadow zone

questions.explanation: The Bay of Bengal branch of the SW Monsoon is forced to rise over the funnel-shaped Khasi Hills, causing intense orographic (relief) rainfall. Mawsynram is the world's wettest place.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Western Disturbances that bring winter rainfall to northwest India originate from:
questions.explanation: Western Disturbances are extratropical cyclones that originate over the Mediterranean Sea. They bring winter rain/snow to J&K, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and fog to the IGP.
questions.subject: Geography

options.option_text: Hot, dry, dust-laden winds blowing from west/northwest in May-June
Cold, moist winds from the Himalayas

questions.explanation: Loo winds: hot (45-48°C), dry, dusty winds blowing from Rajasthan/Punjab towards eastern India in May-June before the monsoon. Can cause fatal heat strokes.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The 'October Heat' phenomenon in India is associated with:

options.option_text: High humidity combined with high temperature as monsoon withdraws in October
Cold wave from Himalayas in October

questions.explanation: As the South-West Monsoon withdraws (October), high temperatures persist but humidity remains high — causing oppressive, uncomfortable conditions called October Heat.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which part of India receives rainfall primarily in winter (November-February)?
questions.explanation: While most of India gets SW Monsoon (summer) rain, Tamil Nadu receives rainfall in winter from the Northeast (Retreating) Monsoon — Bay of Bengal cyclones hit Coromandel Coast.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Amritsar city in Punjab has a more extreme climate than Mumbai despite both being in India because:

options.option_text: Amritsar is inland (continental influence), while Mumbai is coastal (maritime/moderating influence)
Amritsar is in a rain shadow zone

questions.explanation: Distance from sea determines continentality. Coastal cities (Mumbai, Chennai) have moderate temperatures year-round. Inland cities (Delhi, Amritsar) have extreme hot summers and cold winters.
questions.subject: Geography

options.option_text: Thunderstorms (pre-monsoon showers) in West Bengal and northeast India during April-May
A cold wave affecting Assam in winter
A type of cyclone in the Bay of Bengal

questions.explanation: Kalbaisakhi (Bengali: 'kal' = calamity, 'baisakhi' = of Baisakh): violent thunderstorms in WB and NE India in April-May. Useful for jute and tea cultivation.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands experience which type of climate?

options.option_text: Equatorial (hot and humid throughout the year, no distinct dry season)

questions.explanation: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands (near equator, 8-14°N) experience equatorial climate — high rainfall throughout year, high humidity, no distinct dry season.
questions.subject: Geography
